_note: Round 6: the owner's evening tips (sim-core advice.ts). One tip an evening, first in `priority` that holds and is off cooldown (the rota tip never rests). Money is pence. Text placeholders are {name}-style; [[termId|label]] marks a glossary word the game shows as a <Term>.

rota.title: Two weeks of losing money (about {dailyLoss} a day).
rota.body: {name} works {days}, when another {role} is already on. Those shifts cost {weeklyCost} a week. Take them off the [[rota|rota]] until things pick up?
rota.why: The last 14 days lost {totalLoss} in all. {name} is booked for {shifts} doubled-up shifts a week at {shiftCost} each.

overstock.title: You're buying more {ingredientLower} than you can use.
overstock.body: Order less of it, so less of it [[spoilage|goes off]].
overstock.why: In the last {days} days your kitchen used {used} portions of {ingredientLower} and threw away {binned}: {cost} in the bin. It keeps for {shelfLife} days.

dog.title: Hardly anyone orders the {dish}.
dog.body: It's a [[mmDog|dud]]: take it off the menu (fewer things to buy, fewer to go off), or change its price.
dog.why: In {days} days it sold {sold} plates; your other {course}s sold about {courseSold} each. It makes {margin} a plate, they make about {courseMargin}.

idleChef.title: {name} isn't needed on {days}.
idleChef.body: Two chefs cooked fewer plates than one chef manages alone. Give {name} those days off and save {weeklyCost} a week.
idleChef.why: On those days the two chefs cooked at most {plates} plates between them. On {soloDay}, {soloName} cooked {soloPeak} alone.

underpriced.title: Everyone wants to eat here, but you keep very little.
underpriced.body: Put your prices up a little, about {raise}. Busy places can charge a bit more.
underpriced.why: This week about {walkouts} people a night couldn't get a table, and you're very [[popularity|popular]] ({popularity}/100). But over {days} days you {keep}.
